# Starting threads

Starting a thread on a context, its options, and joining it for its result.

<h2 id="thread-options"><code>ThreadOptions</code></h2>

```rux
pub struct ThreadOptions {
    // private fields
```

How a thread is started: its stack size, for now. `Copy`.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Thread/Src/Spawn.rux#L40)

**Methods**

<h3 id="with-stack-size"><code>WithStackSize</code></h3>

```rux
pub func WithStackSize(
    self: &ThreadOptions,
    size: uint
) -> ThreadOptions
```

These options with a stack of `size` bytes. Zero asks for the system's default.
The system rounds the size up to its page size, and refuses one below its minimum.

| Name   | Type   | Description             |
| ------ | ------ | ----------------------- |
| `size` | `uint` | the stack size in bytes |

**Returns**: the changed options

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Thread/Src/Spawn.rux#L49)

<h2 id="join-handle"><code>JoinHandle&lt;R&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub struct JoinHandle<R> {
    // private fields
}
```

A started thread, and the result it will leave.
Joining waits for the thread and hands back what its function returned. Dropping the handle without joining lets
the thread run on and clean up after itself; nothing can then wait for it. A handle is not copied.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Thread/Src/Spawn.rux#L66)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description                     |
| ---- | ------------------------------- |
| `R`  | the type of the thread's result |

**Methods**

<h3 id="join"><code>Join</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Join(self: &var JoinHandle<R>) -> R
```

Waits for the thread to finish and returns what its function returned.
Joining a handle that was already joined or detached is a program error and panics.

**Returns**: the thread's result

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Thread/Src/Spawn.rux#L78)

<h3 id="detach"><code>Detach</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Detach(self: &var JoinHandle<R>)
```

Lets the thread run on without anyone waiting for it. It releases itself, and its result, when it finishes.
Detaching a handle that was already joined or detached does nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Thread/Src/Spawn.rux#L93)

<h3 id="is-joinable"><code>IsJoinable</code></h3>

```rux
pub func IsJoinable(self: &JoinHandle<R>) -> bool
```

Whether the handle can still be joined.

**Returns**: false once it was joined or detached

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Thread/Src/Spawn.rux#L108)

<h2 id="spawn"><code>Spawn&lt;T, R&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Spawn<T: Sendable, R: Sendable>(
    entry: func(T) -> R,
    context: T
) -> JoinHandle<R> ! ThreadError
```

Starts a thread running `entry(context)` with the system's default stack size.
The context moves to the new thread. Whatever `entry` returns waits in the handle until it is joined.
A panic on any thread ends the whole process, as it does on the main one.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Thread/Src/Spawn.rux#L126)

**Type parameters**

| Name          | Description                     |
| ------------- | ------------------------------- |
| `T: Sendable` | the type of the context         |
| `R: Sendable` | the type of the thread's result |

**Parameters**

| Name      | Type           | Description                           |
| --------- | -------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `entry`   | `func(T) -> R` | the function the thread runs          |
| `context` | `T`            | the value the function is called with |

**Returns**: a handle to join the thread with
